- **Above 62,000 MW**: 100% (bid 99 cents, ask 100 cents; 766 contracts in 24 hours)

Prices change with every trade; the [live Kalshi market](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxtxercotpeakd/texas-ercot-peak-electricity-demand/kxtxercotpeakd-26oct04) is the current figure.

## What is our view?

We have no model of our own for this market, so the odds above are the traders' consensus and not an independent estimate. For calibration: in our sample of settled Economics markets, the Kalshi mid-price a day before close scored a Brier error of 0.1108 (a coin-flip price scores 0.25; lower is better).

## How does this market resolve?

> If the highest hourly total system load reported for the ERCOT grid on October 3, 2026 is above 
> 
> 59,000 MW, then the market resolves to Yes.

Close: October 4, 2026 at 04:55 UTC. Expected settlement: October 11, 2026 at 04:56 UTC. Settlement source: [Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT)](https://www.ercot.com/mp/data-products/data-product-details?id=NP6-346-CD). Full terms: [Kalshi contract terms](https://assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/ECONSTAT.pdf).

## What could move the odds?

- The release of the named data series (the settlement source), or a revision to it.
- For daily published series such as gas prices, the latest published value relative to the strike: these series move a fraction of a cent a day, so the odds only swing when the value sits near a strike.
- A rules clarification or settlement-source change published by Kalshi on the market page.
- Order-book depth: thin books move on small orders, so a large price move on little volume says little.

## How reliable are markets like this one?

Across 116 settled Economics markets in our sample (Kalshi, 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-03), the Kalshi mid-price about 24 hours before close had a Brier error of 0.1108; a coin-flip price scores 0.25 and lower is better. Contracts quoted at 5 cents or less settled YES 0% of the time (20 markets); contracts quoted at 95 cents or more settled YES 97% (31 markets). The sample covers a few weeks, so it is a guide to how markets like this have behaved, not a guarantee of how this one will settle.

## Frequently asked questions

### What are the odds on "Texas ERCOT peak electricity demand on Oct 3, 2026"?

As of October 3, 2026 at 20:15 UTC, Kalshi implies Above 62,500 MW at 53%, Above 63,500 MW at 15%, and Above 63,000 MW at 11%. These move with every trade; the live market is at https://kalshi.com/markets/kxtxercotpeakd/texas-ercot-peak-electricity-demand/kxtxercotpeakd-26oct04.

### What does a price on Kalshi mean as a probability?

A contract that pays $1 if the outcome happens and trades at 45 cents implies about a 45% chance, before fees and ignoring the small gap between the bid and the ask. We take the middle of the bid and the ask.

### When does this market close and settle?

It closes October 4, 2026 at 04:55 UTC and is expected to settle October 11, 2026 at 04:56 UTC, in about 9 hours from the time of writing.

### Where does the settlement data come from?

Kalshi names Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) (https://www.ercot.com/mp/data-products/data-product-details?id=NP6-346-CD) as the settlement source. The full contract terms are at https://assets.kalshi.com/contract_terms/ECONSTAT.pdf.

### Can I bet on this on Kalshi?

Kalshi is a federally regulated exchange (a CFTC-designated contract market). Whether you can trade depends on your location and eligibility under Kalshi's terms. The market is at https://kalshi.com/markets/kxtxercotpeakd/texas-ercot-peak-electricity-demand/kxtxercotpeakd-26oct04.

### Is this financial advice?

No. This wire reports a market's odds and its publisher's analysis from public information. Prediction-market contracts can lose their entire price.

object.secondary:
The Expiration Value is the highest value in the TOTAL column of the first complete “Actual System Load by Forecast Zone” CSV report published by ERCOT for the October 3, 2026 operating day.

Each value represents ERCOT system load for the corresponding full hour. Instantaneous load readings displayed elsewhere by ERCOT will not be considered.

Values will be compared as published without rounding. Later revisions, settlement adjustments, or republications will not affect the Expiration Value.
